id: Re-Degradation Reveals Resolution | CVPR 2027 | addendum v6 | registered after run 5 and before run 6
scope: Frozen v1.0 and addenda v2-v5 stay exactly as they are and the 73 checkpoints of runs 1-5 are reused unchanged. Addendum v6 (i) temperature-scales every label-free estimator and plug-in on the labelled source and reports both versions, (ii) defines a label-free attribution score phi and the phi switch, (iii) replaces the AE-LS adapter by a bias-transfer form and adds MaNo with and without the plug-in, (iv) adds block B18 (ImageNet scale: ImageNetV2 as the labelled source, the ImageNet-C definitions on its other half, and the real ImageNet-C blur archive), block B19 (identification compared with blind kernel estimation by KernelGAN) and blocks B20-B23 (temperature-scaled re-runs of B13, B16, B14 and B17 that also save per-image logits), and (v) registers rules Q1-Q12 and the reported analyses Q13-Q17. The paper's claims are reorganised into six claims (claims map below); every rule of v1.0-v6 stays in the ledger with its verdict.
motivation: run 5: no estimator was temperature-scaled, while ATC (Garg et al., ICLR 2022) and COT (Lu et al., NeurIPS 2023) calibrate every method on source validation data. The CIFAR-100 classifiers are 10.6 pp overconfident on clean A2 and raw COT on CIFAR-100-C has 11.7 pp MAE; the linear probes are 7-15 pp overconfident on the harder datasets

run 5, exploratory and post hoc: phi = (c_src(0) - c_src(s_hat)) / (c_src(0) - c_tgt) tracked the labelled share of the accuracy drop explained by blur (Spearman 0.97 over 21 settings, 0.89 over 1,217 cells), and switching the plug-in off for phi < 0.5 removed the LandCover.ai 25 -> 50 cm harm while keeping the CIFAR blur gains. Both are confirmed here only on data that no run has touched (block B18)
run 5: the v5 AE-LS adapter (AE-LS + beta log(1 + s5)) over-corrected on real targets (shifts of -7.8 pp on LandCover.ai and -8.8 pp on fMoW)

reviewers will expect an ImageNet-scale test, the newest accuracy estimator (MaNo, NeurIPS 2024) and a comparison with blind kernel estimation from cross-scale recurrence (Michaeli and Irani, ICCV 2013; Bell-Kligler, Shocher and Irani, NeurIPS 2019)

temperature_scaling.reference: Guo, Pleiss, Sun and Weinberger, ICML 2017
temperature_scaling.fit: one temperature T per classifier (linear probe or trained head): minimise the mean negative log-likelihood of the clean labelled source calibration split A2 over log T in [log 0.05, log 20] (bounded scalar search, tolerance 1e-4)
temperature_scaling.applies_to: every softmax output of every estimator and plug-in: the source at every level, the meta-sets, every target
temperature_scaling.report: pre-T (T = 1, exactly the v1.0-v5 definitions) and post-T; every Q rule uses post-T unless it says otherwise
temperature_scaling.logits: per-image logits (float16) of the clean source and of every target condition are written to the logits folder next to the outputs (not the resume zip); ImageNet targets keep a keyed subset of 1,000 images per condition

plugin_v6.level: as v5: s5 = the v2 level; sigma5 = sigma_v11 only when v1.0 flags the condition and the v2 model check accepts
plugin_v6.AE-LS: bias transfer: AE-LS@s_hat v6 = AE-LS - [b(s5, sigma5) - b(0, 0)], b = the AE-LS prediction on A2 re-degraded to the level (its meta-features read from that set) minus the probe's accuracy there; unclipped predictions inside, the result clipped to [0, 1]
plugin_v6.MaNo: the same bias transfer with the MaNo accuracy prediction
plugin_v6.identity: X@s_hat v6 = X exactly when s5 = 0 and sigma5 = 0, for ATC, ATC-NE, DoC, COT, COTT, AE-LS and MaNo

mano.reference: Xie, Odonnat, Feofanov, Deng, Zhang and An, NeurIPS 2024
mano.score: S = (1/(N K) sum_i sum_k Q_ik^p)^(1/p) with p = 4; Q = softmax(q) when Phi > eta, else the second-order Taylor normalisation (1 + q + q^2/2 minus its row minimum, rows summing to 1); Phi = the mean over images and classes of -log softmax(q) (uniform cross-entropy) on the clean labelled source A2, computed once per classifier and temperature, so that every set of a classifier (meta-sets, source levels, targets) uses the same normalisation (the official code also fixes it once per model); eta = 5
mano.inputs: the classifier's logits on the whole set (temperature-scaled in the post-T version), frozen model in evaluation mode
mano.accuracy: a LinearRegression of accuracy on S over the AutoEval meta-sets, as for NucNorm (the paper reports correlations)

attribution.phi: phi = (c_src(0) - c_src(s5, sigma5)) / (c_src(0) - c_tgt), c = mean maximum softmax probability (post-T); undefined when |c_src(0) - c_tgt| < 0.005
attribution.labelled_share: share = (A_src(0) - A_src(s5, sigma5)) / (A_src(0) - A_tgt), on cells with A_src(0) - A_tgt > 0.02 (evaluation only: it uses target labels)
attribution.switch: X_sw = X@s_hat v6 when phi >= 0.5, else X (also when phi is undefined)

imagenet.source: ImageNetV2 matched-frequency (Recht, Roelofs, Schmidt and Shankar, ICML 2019; 10,000 images, 10 per class; Hugging Face dataset vaishaal/ImageNetV2, file imagenetv2-matched-frequency.tar.gz; label = the folder name, the ImageNet-1k class index)
imagenet.preprocessing: Pillow bilinear resize of the shorter side to 256 and centre crop to 224 (the ImageNet-C preprocessing)
imagenet.split: per class the 10 images ordered by a keyed hash of the file name: the first 5 form A (labelled source, 5,000 images), the other 5 form B (target base, 5,000 images)
imagenet.generated: the nine ImageNet-C families of block B9 (Hendrycks and Dietterich, ICLR 2019) at severities 1-5 applied to B, each image with its own keyed stream, then stored as JPEG quality 85 as the ImageNet-C files were; plus clean B stored as JPEG 85
imagenet.synthetic: B re-degraded in floating point by the heat semigroup: s in {1, 4, 16, 64} px^2 and sigma in {0, 3} DN (keyed noise blocks shared by the pixel stage and every model)
imagenet.real: the ImageNet-C blur archive (Zenodo record 2235448, blur.tar, md5 2d8e81fdd8e07fef67b9334fa635e45c, CC BY 4.0): defocus, glass, motion and zoom blur at severities 1-5; per class the 5 validation images with the smallest keyed hash of the file name (the same 5,000 images in every condition); label = the WordNet folder (sorted wnids = class index). These are ImageNet validation images, a different sample than ImageNetV2, so this target mixes a natural shift with blur
imagenet.model_source: timm, weights from the Hugging Face hub (He et al., CVPR 2016; Liu et al., CVPR 2022; Liu et al., ICCV 2021; Touvron et al., ICML 2021); ImageNet mean/std normalisation; logits from each model's own final linear layer
imagenet.pixel: identification on a keyed subsample of at most 2,000 images per condition (all of B for the synthetic conditions), calibrated on a keyed subsample of 2,000 images of A
imagenet.psf_truth: Gaussian-equivalent PSF variance of the Gaussian and defocus families (corruption_equiv_var of block B9)
imagenet.omitted: the identifier ablation and the known-corruption oracles
imagenet.fresh: no ImageNet image entered any earlier run

kernelgan.method: KernelGAN (Bell-Kligler, Shocher and Irani, NeurIPS 2019) re-implemented from the official code (github.com/sefibk/KernelGAN): deep linear generator with layers [7, 5, 3, 1, 1, 1] and 64 channels (13 x 13 kernel, scale 1/2), 7-layer patch discriminator (7 x 7 then 1 x 1, 64 channels, spectral normalisation), L1 GAN loss, the official constraints and schedule (bicubic 5 with its decay, sum-to-one 0.5, boundaries 0.5, centralised 0 -> 1, sparsity 0 -> 5), Adam 2e-4 with beta1 0.5, 3,000 iterations, learning rate divided by 10 every 750, crops drawn from gradient-weighted probability maps, kernel post-processing with n = 40. N images are trained in parallel with grouped convolutions: every image keeps its own parameters, spectral norms, batch statistics and loss weights
kernelgan.level: Gaussian-equivalent variance of the post-processed kernel (per-axis second moment); per image and per set (median), mapped to px^2 by a monotone calibration on source images re-degraded to known levels; the same source images calibrate s_hat
kernelgan.landcoverai: 8 target tiles (B orthophotos) and 8 calibration tiles (A2 orthophotos), each with the added levels {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16} px^2 (exact DCT heat semigroup)
kernelgan.fmow: 8 keyed target views per gsd bin of block B14 and 8 source crops (A2) at the added levels {0, 1, 2, 4, 8} px^2 for the calibration
kernelgan.comparator: s_hat (v1.0 per-image knees through the same 8-image calibration, set level = median); s_hat with the method's full source calibration is reported

blocks.B23: B17 (the five real pairs, six encoders)

ts_reruns.content: the identification stored in the v5 checkpoint (the same pixels, so the same levels), the same data, splits, classifiers, conditions and random streams; every estimator and plug-in pre-T and post-T; the known-corruption oracles, the identifier ablation and the GSD chain are not repeated
ts_reruns.check: pre-T predictions are compared with the v5 checkpoint (reported, Q17)

Q1.test: identity: every cell of B18 and B20-B23 with s5 = 0 and sigma5 = 0 has X@s_hat v6 = X and X_sw = X exactly for ATC, ATC-NE, DoC, COT, COTT, AE-LS and MaNo, pre-T and post-T

Q2.test: post-T: X@s_hat v6 < X for the 7 pairs, one-sided Wilcoxon on paired cells, Holm over the 7 pairs

Q4.test: post-T: the strongest of the 7 v6 plug-ins against the strongest of the 12 published estimators (the 11 baselines and MaNo), pooled MAE with equal weight per corruption; PASS when the 95% hierarchical bootstrap CI of the difference lies below 0, PARTIAL when it contains 0, FAIL otherwise

Q5.test: post-T, generated targets: X@s_hat v6 < X for the 7 pairs, one-sided Wilcoxon on paired cells (model x condition), Holm over the 7 pairs

Q6.test: Spearman rho between the v2 level and the Gaussian-equivalent PSF variance over the generated Gaussian and defocus conditions (10) >= 0.9 with one-sided p < 0.01, and over the five real-archive defocus conditions >= 0.9; PASS both, PARTIAL one

Q7.settings: generated family (9), synthetic sigma = 0, synthetic sigma = 3 DN, real-archive family (4), each pooled over severities and models; a setting counts when at least 4 of its cells have a labelled drop > 0.02
Q7.test: post-T: Spearman rho between the per-setting median phi and the per-setting median labelled share >= 0.8 with one-sided p < 0.01

Q8.settings: generated blur families, synthetic conditions and the real-archive blur families
Q8.test: post-T: retention = (MAE(X) - MAE(X_sw)) / (MAE(X) - MAE(X@s_hat v6)) >= 0.7 for estimators whose plug-in lowers the pooled MAE; an estimator whose plug-in does not lower it counts as retained when X_sw is not worse than X

Q9.regimes: B23 real pairs without added blur (real_plus0); B22 every fMoW condition
Q9.test: post-T: upper 95% hierarchical bootstrap bound of the pooled X_sw - X <= +0.5 pp for at least 6 of the 7 estimators, on each of the two sets; PASS both, PARTIAL one

Q10.test: post-T, on fMoW (all conditions) and on the real pairs without added blur: AE-LS@s_hat v6 has a lower pooled MAE than the v5 adapter and its upper 95% bound of AE-LS@s_hat v6 - AE-LS is <= +0.5 pp; PASS both sets, PARTIAL one; on FAIL the AE-LS plug-in is reported as a negative result

Q11.test: post-T: MaNo@s_hat v6 < MaNo, one-sided Wilcoxon on paired cells, p < 0.01 in each setting; PASS 3/3, PARTIAL 2/3

Q12.test: (a) LandCover.ai: per-image relative level error |level - s0| / s0 over the five non-zero added levels: s_hat lower than KernelGAN, one-sided Wilcoxon on the paired images p < 0.05 and a lower median; (b) fMoW: Spearman rho of the per-image level with the gsd for s_hat >= that of KernelGAN - 0.05; PASS both, PARTIAL one

reported.Q13: temperatures, NLL and overconfidence per classifier before and after scaling; pre-T vs post-T MAE of every estimator and plug-in per setting
reported.Q14: the v6 plug-in matrix (7 estimators) post-T and pre-T across B18 and B20-B23, and the strongest estimator per setting
reported.Q15: ImageNet real-archive targets (natural shift plus blur): plug-in, switch and blend per family
reported.Q16: phi against the labelled share on B20-B23 (post-T; not fresh data) and the blend
reported.Q17: reproduction: pre-T predictions of B20-B23 against the v5 checkpoints of B13, B16, B14 and B17

Claim 1.statement: Physics: re-degradation by the exact heat semigroup identifies a calibrated blur level (knee law, half-energy law, effective resolution of real 25 vs 50 cm products)

Claim 2.statement: Identification without labels on blur the method did not generate: standard corruption PSFs, real ground-sample-distance and off-nadir shifts, ImageNet scale, and against blind kernel estimation

Claim 3.statement: Plug-in: calibrating a label-free estimator on the source re-degraded to s_hat lowers its error under blur, also after temperature scaling and at ImageNet scale

Claim 4.statement: No harm by construction: the plug-in is an exact identity when no blur is identified

Claim 5.statement: Attribution: phi estimates without labels how much of an accuracy drop blur explains, and the phi switch keeps the blur gains without harming other shifts

Claim 6.statement: Boundaries: on real sensor shifts where blur is a minority of the shift, the plug-in helps confidence-based estimators and not distribution-matching ones
